clue.text: Minister takes risk with spin going round

parts.note: to take a risk is to take a chance

indicators.note: going round means the word for spin turns about and is read backwards

parts.note: a spin is a roll, as of a ball or a die

explanation.surface: A government minister gambles by sending everything into a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' looks like the minister's PR, but it is a roll. The Chancellor of the Exchequer is the UK finance minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is a senior cabinet member in Britain, a government office-holder.

clue.text: Mange to get something for priest to wear

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Mange to get something for priest to wear (4)': 'Mange' does not mean COPE; almost certainly a slip for 'Manage' (double definition), but no source confirms the printed text
annotationWithheld.clue: Mange to get something for priest to wear

clue.text: But date may go wrong if one's touched!

indicators.note: may go wrong suggests the letters of the two words beside it are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that a date may fall through if someone is a bit mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touched' looks like 'a bit mad', but it means 'in contact with'. 'may go wrong' rearranges BUT DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that border each other share an edge, so to have abutted is to have been in contact.

clue.text: Musician playing in recitals outside front of theatre repeatedly

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled letters go round the other piece
playing suggests the letters of in recitals are being played about with into a new order
repeatedly means the single letter taken from theatre is used twice over
front of picks just the opening letter of the word theatre

explanation.surface: A musician performs in recitals, standing outside the theatre entrance again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing in recitals' looks like a concert, but 'in' is fodder. 'repeatedly' doubles the letter that 'front of' takes, and 'outside' wraps the rearranged letters round that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet player is an instrumentalist, one kind of performer of music.

clue.text: Relaxed having got left with help and support

parts.note: to help is to aid
to support someone is to back them

explanation.surface: Someone is calm, having been given help and support.
explanation.definitionFit: A laid-back person is easy-going and unhurried, an informal idiom for calm.

clue.text: All 18 holes given good exposure

parts.note: a golf course's front nine holes are called the out and the back nine the in, so together they make all eighteen
the second half of a golf round, the back nine, is called the in

explanation.surface: A golfer's full round brings good publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf the first nine holes are 'out' and the last nine 'in', so the whole course gives OUT + IN; G is good.
explanation.definitionFit: Being publicly revealed, as when someone's private life is made known, is an exposure of that kind.

clue.text: Record is lodged in federal district

indicators.note: lodged in means the little word is is stuck inside the other piece

parts.note: DC is the District of Columbia, the US federal district

explanation.surface: A record is filed in Washington DC.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat round platter of vinyl, so a record is one.

clue.text: Pitch in when encountering Conservative policy

parts.note: a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: Someone joins in when meeting Tory policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch here is a slope, as of a roof, which is a gradient or slant.

clue.text: Accountant continued to want posh car

parts.note: a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce, the classic luxury car

explanation.surface: An accountant kept wanting an expensive car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to want' is only a link. 'Roller' is British slang for a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: A financial controller is the senior bookkeeper who oversees a firm's finances.

clue.text: For them living is not enough

definitions.text: For them living is not enough

parts.words: For them living is not enough
parts.note: a living is a church benefice; some clergy held several livings at once, which a single one was not enough for

explanation.surface: People for whom merely being alive does not satisfy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'living' looks like being alive, but it is a clergyman's benefice; holders of more than one were so named.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, clergy who held more than one benefice at the same time were given this name.

clue.text: Look at colt brought into school hospital

indicators.note: brought into means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a san, short for sanatorium, is the sickbay at a boarding school
C is the abbreviation for colt in racing form

explanation.surface: Someone examines a young horse brought into the school sickbay.
explanation.walkthrough: SAN (sanatorium) is the British boarding-school sickbay.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to examine or read over, a synonym for inspect.

clue.text: Retaliation from buffoon hiding under work surface

indicators.note: hiding under places the buffoon's word beneath the work surface in this down clue

parts.note: a counter is a kitchen or shop work surface
Mr Punch is the clownish puppet of Punch and Judy shows

explanation.surface: A comic figure hides beneath the kitchen worktop to get revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'hiding under' puts PUNCH below COUNTER. Punch is the clown puppet of British seaside Punch and Judy shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterpunch is a blow struck back in reply, a return attack.

clue.text: Case that is put back involves trade union

indicators.note: involves means the reversed piece wraps around the union's letters
put back means the abbreviation for that is is read in reverse

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A legal case is reopened and drags in the union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks legal, but it is a container. 'put back' reverses the abbreviation before 'involves' wraps it round the union.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental holder for needles or sewing tools, so a kind of container.

clue.text: Lad in robe fixed with special belt

indicators.note: fixed suggests the letters of lad in robe are mended into another order

explanation.surface: A boy in a gown is fitted with a particular belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges LAD IN ROBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolier is a shoulder strap with pockets or loops for carrying cartridges.

clue.text: German city graduate gets to study more than once

indicators.note: more than once means the graduate and study pair is repeated

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A graduate ends up studying over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than once' doubles BA + DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Baden-Baden is a spa town in south-west Germany's Black Forest.

clue.text: One enthralled by poet joining church people at event

indicators.note: enthralled by means the single letter is held captive inside the poet's name

parts.note: W H Auden was an English poet
I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A listener is captivated by a poet whose work is linked to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: W H Auden was an Anglo-American poet; 'enthralled by' holds the one inside his name, and CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is the crowd of spectators or listeners gathered for a show.

clue.text: Maybe remove the waxy stuff from a foreign animal

parts.note: un is French for a, the indefinite article in a foreign language
a seal is a marine animal

explanation.surface: Someone may scrape wax off a creature from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a foreign' is the indefinite article in French, UN. 'Maybe' marks the definition as an example: breaking a wax seal is one way of opening something.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking the wax that closes a letter is one way to open it, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Adhesive to bond in a second window frame

indicators.note: in means the letters for a second go inside the adhesive's word

parts.note: cement is an adhesive

explanation.surface: Glue is used to fix a window frame in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bond' is link words; 'in' puts A S inside CEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a hinged sash, the frame of a window that opens like a door.

clue.text: Mannered English female going to gala

parts.note: a fete is a gala or fair

explanation.surface: A refined Englishwoman goes to a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: A FETE is a British summer fair, usually outdoors with stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means affected and over-refined, which is what mannered describes.

clue.text: Limp little creature put up in front of detectives

indicators.note: put up means the creature's word reads upwards, backwards in this down clue

parts.note: a calf is a young animal
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detectives

explanation.surface: A drooping small animal is held up before the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns CALF into FLAC in a down entry; CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaccid means floppy and lacking firmness, which describes something drooping.

clue.text: Observe what someone at the till will often do

definitions.text: what someone at the till will often do

explanation.surface: A shop assistant pays attention when cash is handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to pay attention; a cashier at the till accepts banknotes.

clue.text: Son in difficulties meets hero swimming towards the beach

indicators.note: in difficulties suggests the letters of son are thrown into disorder
swimming suggests the letters of hero move around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A struggling son meets a hero swimming to shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in difficulties' rearranges SON into ONS; 'swimming' rearranges HERO into HORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Onshore means moving landward, from the sea to the coast.

clue.text: Foreign city where you may see archdeacon skating?

parts.note: Ven, the Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
skating is done on ice, so the skater is on top of it

explanation.surface: Imagining a churchman on skates in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated VEN; skating puts him on ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice is the Italian city of canals, abroad from a British view.

clue.text: Money one needs before getting something in womenswear

parts.note: brass is northern English slang for money
I is the Roman numeral one
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A person needs cash before buying clothes for women.
explanation.walkthrough: BRASS is northern British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is a bra, a ladies' undergarment.

clue.text: Matter that's nasty, hot and offensive

definitions.note: here a noun, a military attack

parts.note: pus is the unpleasant matter from an infected wound
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant is described as nasty, hot and disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' reads as an adjective but is the noun: a military advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A push is a concerted military advance, an attack on the enemy.

clue.text: Notice the man at the top, a leader

indicators.note: at the top means the man's word sits above the notice in this down clue

parts.note: he is the man
an ad, an advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: A notice says the man at the top is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'at the top' puts HE above AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a chief or principal, the person in charge.

clue.text: Weed in watery area

explanation.surface: A weed growing in a wet place.
explanation.definitionFit: Dock is a broad-leaved plant; a dock is also an enclosed basin of water for ships.

clue.text: Coo! Is that what you can get in here?

definitions.text: Coo! Is that what you can get in here?

parts.words: Coo! Is that what you can get in here?
parts.note: coo is the sound a dove makes, so the whole clue asks what small compartment a cooing bird could fit into

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at what is available in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coo!' looks like an exclamation of surprise but is the bird's call, pointing to a bird-sized hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeonhole is a small compartment in a desk, named after nesting holes in a dovecote.

clue.text: Poke not good for someone very much exposed

indicators.note: not means the letter for good is left out

parts.note: to poke is to nudge

explanation.surface: A jab that isn't nice for someone very vulnerable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes G from NUDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A naked person, without clothes, is as uncovered as can be.

clue.text: The dial he's twiddled is feature of spaceship

indicators.note: twiddled suggests the letters of the dial he's are turned about into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters H E S

explanation.surface: A man fiddles with a dial on a spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twiddled' rearranges THE DIAL HES.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat shield protects a spacecraft from burning up on re-entry into the atmosphere.
